flagged.evidence: [L1] says that one quotient block's member blocks can be listed as $A_1,\dots,A_t$ with every consecutive pair mixed. The cited definitions only give that the member blocks form one mixed-block reachability class, i.e. any two are joined by some mixed chain. They do not imply a single ordering of all members with consecutive mixed pairs. Counterexample: take four original blocks $A,B,C,D$ with mixed pairs exactly $(A,B)$, $(B,C)$, and $(B,D)$, and all other pairs anticomplete. Then all four blocks lie in one $\mathcal M$-class, hence one quotient block, but no ordering of $A,B,C,D$ has every consecutive pair mixed; such an ordering would be a Hamiltonian path in the star $K_{1,3}$, which does not exist. So [L1] states a stronger and false combinatorial property, and the proof steps built on it are not licensed.

Step 3.1 attributes to [L2] the specific witness choice `x'=y`, `y'=u`, and `any choice of u'\in B`. But the opened dependency `lem-a-quotient-mixed-block-witness-descends-to-two-member-blocks` states only that there exist vertices `x',y',u'` with the required properties; its Statement does not identify them with `y,u`, nor does it say that every vertex of `B` works. So 3.1 cites [L2] for conclusions not present in the cited Statement.
